metadata.title: Variational Helium — Screened Nuclear Charge Z*
metadata.purpose: Critique of qmcg-variational-helium: energy landscape, unit bug on Z*, rubber-stamp bound checker

beats.narration_text: Salut. Liam — in for Bear. Someone handed Claude one prompt: write me a visualization for variational helium, screened nuclear charge Z-star. Here's what came back. We're judging the viz, not the physics.

props.command: Hey Claude, write me a visualization for variational helium — screened nuclear charge Z*.
props.segment: Variational Helium — Screened Nuclear Charge Z*
output: ✓ D3 CDN — four overlapping energy curves

beats.narration_text: White page, two columns. Left: a D3 plot — Z-star from 0.5 to 3.0 on the x-axis, energy in Hartree on the y. Five curves: a solid red total-energy parabola, three dashed component lines for kinetic, nuclear, and electron-electron terms, and a dashed horizontal reference at the exact helium ground state. A draggable red dot rides the parabola; a vertical guide drops to the axis. Below the chart: a slider and a Minimize button. Right: a live numerical panel, a static minimum summary, and a physics console.

The slider drives Z-star — the effective nuclear charge in the trial wavefunction psi proportional to e to the negative Z-star r. Drag left toward 0.5: the wavefunction spreads, nuclear attraction falls, but kinetic energy falls faster — the total energy climbs steeply. Drag right past 2.0: kinetic energy grows quadratically and the total climbs again. The minimum at Z-star equals 27 over 16 is where those competing forces balance. Every component — kinetic, nuclear, electron-electron repulsion — updates live in the panel.

Three things land. One: the simultaneous overlay of four curves — kinetic, nuclear, electron-electron, and total — makes the variational argument visible as geometry. You can see kinetic energy rise quadratically while nuclear attraction falls linearly; their competition determines where the minimum sits. Two: the live panel updates synchronously — at Z-star equals 1.0, kinetic energy reads exactly 1.0000 Hartree, nuclear attraction reads negative 4.0000. Spot-verifiable by hand from the closed-form expressions. Three: the hollow minimum marker pre-labels Z-star equals 27 over 16 before you drag to it. The label is a prediction, not a caption.
beats.new_visual_element: SOURCE-CUT: media/output.mp4 pros beat — full default view

beats.narration_text: Three problems. First: Z-star in the panel is labeled Eh to the one-half — square root of Hartree. Z-star is dimensionless. Wrong unit on the central variable, every frame. Second: the bound checker — the green tag reading variational principle satisfied — can never turn red. The analytical minimum of this trial function is negative 2.8477, which is always 56 milliHartree above the exact energy. The check cannot fail by construction; students learn the bound is always guaranteed, which is a property of this one trial family, not the variational principle at large. Third: the three component curves run at opacity 0.55 in near-identical grays. On screen, kinetic from nuclear from electron-electron repulsion is barely distinguishable without the legend.
beats.new_visual_element: SOURCE-CUT: media/change.mp4 full sweep — unit bug and dim curves visible throughout

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Useful after the analytic derivation — shows the energy parabola, verifiable numbers, the minimum pre-marked. But Z-star is labeled with the wrong unit — Eh to the one-half on a dimensionless parameter. The bound checker always stays green, so it teaches a guarantee specific to this trial function, not the variational principle in general. The component curves are barely distinguishable. Fix the unit first.

artifactLines: Energy parabola with verifiable component curves
Component curves: near-identical grays at opacity 0.55

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I have a variational helium D3 simulation. Three fixes needed. First: the Z-star display appends the unit Eh to the one-half, but Z-star is a dimensionless screening parameter — remove the unit string entirely. Second: the three component curves — kinetic energy Z-star squared, nuclear attraction negative 4 Z-star, and electron-electron repulsion 5 eighths Z-star — are all opacity 0.55 in shades of gray. Assign each a distinct color and raise opacity to 0.8 so students can trace individual terms without the legend. Third: add a one-line italic note — fixed, independent of slider — to the Minimum Point panel header so first-time users know it does not track the slider. Return the minimal HTML changes for all three.
